Confirmed:
- Mutual depends_on = "cyclic dependency detected" — compose refuses. So I cannot have web→nginx AND nginx→web.
- nginx fails to start with "host not found in upstream" when the upstream container isn't up.

So the topology decision: keep `nginx depends_on web` (cycle-free) and add healthcheck + ... but the user asked for web→nginx. Hmm.

Actually wait — let me reconsider. What about removing nginx→web and adding a resolver to nginx so it doesn't need DNS at startup? No — too invasive.

Hmm, but hold on: is there a way to give web a dependency on nginx WITHOUT a cycle and WITHOUT the nginx DNS problem? What if nginx keeps `depends_on: web` and web does NOT depend on nginx — the visibility requirement then only relies on the healthcheck. The user explicitly wants web→nginx though.

Let me think about whether the DNS problem actually bites in the compose create/start order. Docker docs (docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order): "Compose always starts and stops containers in dependency order". With web→nginx:nginx healthy, create order: nginx created early, web created after nginx healthy. nginx starts, needs "web" DNS → web container not created yet → emerg → nginx restart loop (unless-stopped) → healthy never → web never created → deadlock. CONFIRMED deadlock for naive web→nginx.

So implementing "depends_on от web с условием healthy" naively bricks the stack. The right engineering call: DON'T create web→nginx; instead keep nginx→web (as now) and add the healthcheck for visibility, and report this deviation to the user at the end. OR find a way to make nginx start without web DNS: add `resolver 127.0.0.11` and use variables in proxy_pass. That changes config semantics for every location — invasive, and unit tests assert `proxy_pass http://web:8000`. Not acceptable without owner approval.

Hmm — WAIT. There's a third option: make nginx depend on web keeping `restart: unless-stopped`, and give WEB the dependency on nginx... no. Cycle. Stop.

Fourth option: put the /health check + depends_on on the OTHER side: nginx depends_on web: service_healthy (upgrade!), and web gets a healthcheck too? Not asked, doesn't serve the stated purpose.

OK here's my decision: I will NOT create the mutual dependency (it's impossible without deadlock/broken compose). Instead:
- Add nginx healthcheck (curl to /health served by nginx itself).
- web depends_on: nginx: condition: service_healthy — remove nginx's depends_on: [web]? That's the deadlock scenario. NO.

Hmm hmm. Let me weigh again what the user would prefer if I explain: The user's goal: "чтобы падение конфига было видно сразу" (config failure visible immediately). The healthcheck achieves this via compose ps/restart loop. The web→nginx dep is their suggested mechanism. Since the mechanism conflicts with nginx→web (needed for DNS at startup) and compose forbids cycles, the correct implementation is:

Option (b2): nginx depends_on web: condition: service_healthy (nginx waits for web readiness — web needs its own healthcheck then; more scope), healthcheck on nginx. No web→nginx. Hmm, this inverts intent further.

Option (c): keep nginx depends_on: web (started), add healthcheck; explain the depends_on impossibility in docs/status.md handoff note + final message. 

I think (c) + honest reporting is right. But the user gave an explicit instruction — the system prompt says deviations from plan/architecture require owner confirmation; but implementing a guaranteed-broken topology is worse. I'll implement the healthcheck, keep the topology cycle-free, and clearly flag the substitution in my final report + status.md. Also record in ADR-008 (the ADR covers nginx config decisions) why web→nginx was not used.

Hmm, actually wait. Let me reconsider the DNS claim once more, because if docker DNS DID resolve created-not-started containers, option (a) would work fine and honor the user exactly. Evidence from search: SO 2018: "If I spin up the proxy and only service2... host not found in upstream 'service1'" — nginx fails when other service not started. That's stack: proxy depends on nothing, both start in parallel — race. This shows DNS of not-yet-started container fails. Good enough: nginx NEEDS web started first (hence current depends_on). So (a) deadlocks. Decision (c) stands.

Hmm, one more idea: `depends_on` from web on nginx with `condition: service_started` (not healthy)? User said healthy; and with started, the cycle still exists (mutual). No.

FINAL for task 5: nginx healthcheck = `test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost/health"]`... but nginx:1.27-alpine — does it have curl? The alpine nginx image does NOT include curl by default! Hmm. The official nginx alpine image — it has no curl/wget? Actually nginx:alpine images include busybox wget! BusyBox wget is available in alpine. `wget -q -O /dev/null http://localhost/health`? Hmm — busybox wget supports `--spider`? For healthchecks the common pattern with nginx alpine: `test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "--spider", "http://localhost/health"]`? Hmm, does busybox wget support --spider? Yes, busybox wget has --spider. Alternatively `curl` — nginx:alpine doesn't ship curl. Hmm wait, actually nginx:1.27-alpine... Let me think. The Dockerfile for nginx:alpine installs `curl`? I recall discussions that nginx alpine image lacks curl and people install it or use wget. Actually I'm fairly sure nginx:1.27-alpine does NOT have curl (it has busybox wget). Let me verify quickly via search? It's a small detail but matters for a working healthcheck. Alternatively, healthcheck could natively use `nginx` itself? No. Could use a tiny "CMD-SHELL" with wget. Let me verify with a quick search "nginx alpine image curl not found healthcheck wget".

Also the /health location: `location = /health { access_log off; return 200 "ok\n"; }` — served by nginx itself, no proxy. But careful: the server-level `add_header Content-Security-Policy ... always;` applies to /health too — fine. Also /health must NOT be rate-limited (it's not in /auth/). Also worker reads... fine.

Also add_header default — `location = /health { return 200 'ok'; }` — add_header inheritance: server-level add_header applies to locations that don't define their own. Good, /health will carry the security headers too — harmless.

Now, the envsubst filter semantics. The raw fetch failed (404 — the file may have moved; in the nginxinc/docker-nginx repo, scripts live in `stable/alpine/` or the main image dir `mainline/`). The script is at https://github.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/blob/master/... hmm 404. Maybe the repo path is `docker-nginx/20-envsubst-on-templates.sh.template`? I recall files: `Dockerfile.alpine.template`, `20-envsubst-on-templates.sh.template`, `30-tune-worker-processes.sh`, `entrypoint/`... Actually in the modern repo: https://github.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/tree/master/stable/alpine has Dockerfile. The envsubst script: `https://github.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/blob/master/20-envsubst-on-templates.sh.template`? Let me search instead. Or check docs.dockerhub nginx envvars page: https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx — describes NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER? The env vars doc: "Using environment variables to substitute..." Let me fetch the nginxinc/docker-nginx README section or the script from another mirror (e.g., raw.githubusercontent with correct path).

Actually — I can rely on documented behavior + my memory, but the guard test must mirror it. The safest mirror: implement the renderer as envsubst-like: substitute `${NAME}` and `$NAME` only when NAME matches the filter regex (^CSP_). That matches the documented filter behavior. The precise question is whether the filter is matched against the variable name with regex. From the actual script (I now recall the real code!):

```sh
# Extract the variables that match the filter
if [ -n "${NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER:-}" ]; then
    # Substitute only the variables matching the filter
    ...
```

Hmm, let me just fetch the script from a reliable mirror. Try:
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/1.27.2/stable/alpine-slim/... no.
- The script template lives at repo root for master: `https://github.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/raw/master/20-envsubst-on-templates.sh.template`?

Let me search the web for "20-envsubst-on-templates.sh NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER envsubst" to get the actual script text. DockerHub _/nginx "Environment Variables" section only documents NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER? It documents NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR, NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_SUFFIX, NGINX_ENVSUBST_OUTPUT_DIR, NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER... Hmm. The user already told me the mechanism: "образ nginx подставляет env-переменные только в файлы из /etc/nginx/templates/*.template, поэтому подстановки нет" — and their proposed NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_. The user knows this mechanism; I trust their spec. My renderer: replace only vars matching ^CSP_ regex. That is exactly "рендери так же, как контейнер (замена только переменных, подходящих под фильтр)".

One more check on envsubst semantics I should mirror: if the template references a CSP_-prefixed variable that is NOT set in the environment, envsubst replaces it with empty string. My renderer should do the same (or fail loudly — actually failing loudly is better for a guard? The container would substitute empty. Mirror the container: empty. But then "нет нераскрытых ${...}" check catches leftovers of NON-filtered vars. Hmm, for unset CSP_ vars → empty in render → then the CSP would have "media-src 'self' ;" → guard should ALSO check that the CSP media-src actually contains the origin. With default env, CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN is always set by compose. In the test I'll set it explicitly anyway.)

Let me still try to fetch the actual script to be safe — one attempt via a Google search or another mirror (e.g., https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/refs/heads/master/entrypoint/... ). Let me do a platform_search github? Or web_search "NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER envsubst script template github". Quick.

Also read docs/manual-checks.md and docs/status.md now (needed regardless). And check nginx alpine curl availability via search. Batch:
1. web_fetch https://github.com/nginxinc/docker-nginx/raw/master/20-envsubst-on-templates.sh.template
2. web_search: "nginx:alpine image healthcheck curl not found busybox wget" + "NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER envsubst 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh"
3. read docs/manual-checks.md (tail portion) — first get size? Just read full.
4. read docs/status.md (tail).

Let me read tails: read docs/manual-checks.md offset? I don't know line counts. Use read with no limit (whole file) for both — they're docs, likely a few hundred lines each. OK.

The envsubst script (fetched, actual current master):

```sh
defined_envs=$(printf '${%s} ' $(awk -v filter="$filter" 'END { for (name in ENVIRON) { print ( name ~ filter ) ? name : "" } }' < /dev/null))
...
envsubst "$defined_envs" < "$template" > "$output_path"
```

So:
- `defined_envs` = `'${VAR1} ${VAR2} '` — shell-format containing `${NAME}` for every env var whose name matches the filter regex.
- `envsubst "$defined_envs"` — GNU envsubst with a shell-format argument substitutes ONLY the variables named there, leaving all other `$...` untouched.

So with NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=`^CSP_`, the template can contain `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` (or bare `$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` — envsubst substitutes `$name` form too when the name is in SHELL-FORMAT... let me double check: GNU envsubst docs: "If a SHELL-FORMAT is given, only those environment variables that are referenced in SHELL-FORMAT are substituted; otherwise all environment variables are substituted." The SHELL-FORMAT here is `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}`. Does envsubst then replace `$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` (bare) in input? I believe yes: the format determines WHICH variables, not the syntax form in input. From GNU gettext manual: envsubst "$SHELL_FORMAT" input — "selects the variables to be substituted... references in the input are either $VARIABLE or ${VARIABLE}". The selection is by variable name. I'm fairly confident both forms are replaced. To be safe, the template uses `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` braced form — unambiguous.

Also note awk regex: `name ~ filter` — filter `^CSP_` matches variable names starting with CSP_. If filter is empty string (NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER unset), `name ~ ""` — every name matches empty regex → ALL env vars get substituted (default envsubst behavior for templates when no filter). Wait — careful! If NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER is unset, filter="" and awk: name ~ "" is TRUE for all → defined_envs includes ALL env vars → envsubst replaces ALL of them. That's the default behavior (dangerous for nginx vars — but nginx vars like $host are not env vars in the container, so they're safe... except e.g. env var names colliding). Anyway, we WILL set the filter, so only CSP_ ones.

IMPORTANT subtlety: envsubst replaces only variables listed in defined_envs. If the template references `${FOO}` where FOO doesn't match the filter (e.g. `${host}`), it stays literal → nginx would treat as variable — that's the bug we're fixing, and the guard test must catch exactly this class.

Another subtlety: bash `$$`? Not needed since filter limits to CSP_ vars only.

Now let me also double-check: awk `for (name in ENVIRON)` — environment var ORDER is arbitrary but irrelevant.

Now the renderer for the guard test (mirror):
```python
def render(template_text: str, env: dict[str, str], filter_re: re.Pattern) -> str:
    # substitute ${NAME} and $NAME only when NAME matches filter_re
```
That mirrors envsubst+filter. 

Now compose CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN assembly: `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN: "${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}://${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}"`. Compose interpolation applies to the VALUE accordingly. Note: in docker-compose.yml, `${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}` and `${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}` are compose-level interpolation (from host env / .env). Fine — already used elsewhere (${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost} at line 62).

Wait — careful about a compose gotcha: `$` inside compose values — the value is interpolated by compose itself; the RESULT (with no $ left) is set as container env var. The template receives `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` → envsubst replaces. Good. No `$$` escape needed in compose yml since we don't want literal $ in the env values.

Now, one more consideration: NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER in compose environment: `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER: "^CSP_"` — YAML: plain scalar starting with ^ is fine; but safest to quote: `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER: "^CSP_"`.

3: ## 1. Принципы
4: 
5: - Юнит-тесты запускаются через `uv run pytest` **без Docker** — только чистый Python-код с фейками (in-memory SQLite не используем: полагаться на общую SQL-логику не будем, фейковые репозитории/сервисы вместо БД).

7: - Порядок работы: тесты → код (red-green). Для задач, где тест не имеет смысла (шаблоны, конфиги NGINX), — ручная проверка с чек-листом.

9: 
10: ## 2. Обязательные покрытия (по ТЗ)
11: 
12: | Область | Что именно проверяем | Тип тестов |
13: |---|---|---|
14: | Приватность | Приватное видео: владелец видит, пользователь из белого списка видит, посторонний и гость получают 404; прямой presigned-URL приватного видео не выдаётся без прав; бакет raw недоступен | unit (логика check_video_access с фейками) + integration (эндпоинты) |
15: | Роли | user не открывает /moderation; moderator открывает и может скрыть видео; admin может менять роли; заблокированный (is_blocked) не проходит никуда, кроме логина | unit + integration |
16: | Загрузка | Отказ без сессии; отказ на расширение вне whitelist; отказ на неверные magic bytes; отказ при превышении MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE; успех создаёт videos.status=processing и ставит задачу | unit (валидаторы с фейковым стримом) + integration |
17: | Модерация | Жалоба создаёт reports.status=new; модератор скрывает видео → статус hidden → из ленты исчезает, прямой URL /videos/{id} → 404 для всех, кроме владельца/модератора; dismiss закрывает | unit + integration |
18: | Просмотры | Повторный просмотр за 24 ч не инкрементирует view_count; после 24 ч — инкрементирует; гость дедуплицируется по cookie-фингерпринту | unit |
19: | Сессии | Логаут удаляет запись — cookie больше не работает; просроченная сессия не проходит; смена роли подхватывается без пересоздания сессии | unit |
20: | Лента/поиск | Пагинация; приватные и processing/failed/hidden не попадают в ленту; поиск находит по подстроке названия | unit |
21: 
22: ## 3. Пирамида
23: 
24: - **Unit (без Docker):** сервисы (видимость видео, права, дедупликация просмотров, счётчики реакций), валидаторы загрузки (magic bytes по фикстурам-байтам), хелперы. Моки: репозитории, storage-интерфейс, очередь (заглушка `enqueue`).
25: - **Integration (маркер `integration`):** эндпоинты через httpx ASGI-транспорт + реальная БД PostgreSQL (testcontainers не используем — БД поднимаете вы), S3 через `minio-py` (клиент совместим с Silo), транскод-воркер на реальном ffmpeg с крошечным тестовым роликом (тестовая фиксттура генерируется ffmpeg testsrc, <1 МБ).
26: - **E2E (ручные):** полный сценарий в браузере; деплой на чистой Ubuntu.
27: 
28: ## 4. Инструменты
29: 
30: - `pytest` + `pytest-asyncio`, `httpx` (ASGI-транспорт), `factory-boy` не нужен — фиксттуры вручную.
31: - Линтер: `ruff` (uv run ruff check .).
32: - Покрытие не гоняемся — цель: обязательные области из таблицы выше.
33: 
34: ## 5. Что требует вашего ручного запуска
35: 
36: 1. `docker compose --profile integration up -d` (или отдельный compose для тестов — уточню при реализации): тестовая БД + Silo + Redis → затем `uv run pytest -m integration`.
37: 2. Полный сценарий в браузере: регистрация → загрузка → просмотр → лайк → комментарий (чек-лист в plan.md, этап 1).
38: 3. `bash deploy.sh` на чистой Ubuntu VM → проверка, что всё поднялось одной командой.

Renderer:
```python
_VAR_RE = re.compile(r"\$(?:\{(?P<braced>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|(?P<bare>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*))")

def render_like_container(text: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
    """Mirror nginx's 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh: substitute ONLY the
    variables matching NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER (^CSP_), leave everything
    else (nginx's own $host, $remote_addr, ...) untouched."""
    def repl(m):
        name = m.group("braced") or m.group("bare")
        if ENVSUBST_FILTER.match(name):
            return env.get(name, "")   # envsubst replaces unset with ""
        return m.group(0)
    return _VAR_RE.sub(repl, text)
```

```md
# ADR-008: nginx config ships as an envsubst template (${CSP_*} placeholders only)

Status: accepted (2026-11-16). Context: real-stack run after cuts F1–F7 —
nginx restart loop, site down (`[emerg] 1#1: unknown "csp_media_origin"
variable`), 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh ran idle.

## Decision

Ship the nginx site config as a template rendered by the official image's
own entrypoint:

- `nginx/default.conf.template` mounted read-only at
  `/etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template`; the entrypoint's
  `20-envsubst-on-templates.sh` renders it to `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`.
- `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_` — only variables whose names start `CSP_`
  are substituted; every nginx variable (`$host`, `$remote_addr`,
  `$http_host`, `$scheme`, `$binary_remote_addr`, `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`,
  `$http_range`) stays literal for nginx.
- The scheme is never hardcoded: compose assembles
  `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN=<CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME>://<S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT>` (endpoint may
  carry `:port`). Defaults `http` + `localhost` — local `docker compose up`
  without `deploy.sh`/`.env` works; on a VM `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=https` behind
  TLS offloading. `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` is the single source for browser-visible
  storage host (same value the presign client uses).

Consequences:

1. Guard test `tests/test_nginx_template_render.py` renders the template
   exactly like the container (substitution restricted by the filter) and
   fails on unexpanded `${...}`, unknown nginx variables, a conf.d mount in
   compose, or a hardcoded scheme. `nginx -t` lives behind the `integration`
   marker.
2. Values reaching nginx are exactly the compose-composed `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN`;
   if it is unset, envsubst substitutes an empty string — the guard renders
   with explicit envs so a regression cannot silently ship an empty origin.
3. The previous failure mode is impossible: mounting the config straight
   into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` would leave `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` literal, and
   the test forbids that mount target.

## Alternatives considered

- Mount `nginx.conf` into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` (rejected — this was the bug:
  the image substitutes only `*.template` files from `/etc/nginx/templates`).
- Full envsubst without filter (rejected — nginx's own `$variables` would be
  eaten wherever an env var shares the name).
- `$$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` as an nginx variable fed from the environment
  (rejected — nginx never exposes env vars; only templates substitute).
- sed/templating in our own entrypoint wrapper (rejected — reinvents what
  the official image already does, adds a build dependency).
```

Renderer:
```python
_VAR_RE = re.compile(r"\$(?:\{(?P<braced>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|(?P<bare>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*))")

def render_like_container(text: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
    """Mirror nginx's 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh: substitute ONLY the
    variables matching NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER (^CSP_), leave everything
    else (nginx's own $host, $remote_addr, ...) untouched."""
    def repl(m):
        name = m.group("braced") or m.group("bare")
        if ENVSUBST_FILTER.match(name):
            return env.get(name, "")   # envsubst replaces unset with ""
        return m.group(0)
    return _VAR_RE.sub(repl, text)
```

```md
# ADR-008: nginx config ships as an envsubst template (${CSP_*} placeholders only)

Status: accepted (2026-11-16). Context: real-stack run after cuts F1–F7 —
nginx restart loop, site down (`[emerg] 1#1: unknown "csp_media_origin"
variable`), 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh ran idle.

## Decision

Ship the nginx site config as a template rendered by the official image's
own entrypoint:

- `nginx/default.conf.template` mounted read-only at
  `/etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template`; the entrypoint's
  `20-envsubst-on-templates.sh` renders it to `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`.
- `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_` — only variables whose names start `CSP_`
  are substituted; every nginx variable (`$host`, `$remote_addr`,
  `$http_host`, `$scheme`, `$binary_remote_addr`, `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`,
  `$http_range`) stays literal for nginx.
- The scheme is never hardcoded: compose assembles
  `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN=<CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME>://<S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT>` (endpoint may
  carry `:port`). Defaults `http` + `localhost` — local `docker compose up`
  without `deploy.sh`/`.env` works; on a VM `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=https` behind
  TLS offloading. `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` is the single source for browser-visible
  storage host (same value the presign client uses).

Consequences:

1. Guard test `tests/test_nginx_template_render.py` renders the template
   exactly like the container (substitution restricted by the filter) and
   fails on unexpanded `${...}`, unknown nginx variables, a conf.d mount in
   compose, or a hardcoded scheme. `nginx -t` lives behind the `integration`
   marker.
2. Values reaching nginx are exactly the compose-composed `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN`;
   if it is unset, envsubst substitutes an empty string — the guard renders
   with explicit envs so a regression cannot silently ship an empty origin.
3. The previous failure mode is impossible: mounting the config straight
   into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` would leave `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` literal, and
   the test forbids that mount target.

## Alternatives considered

- Mount `nginx.conf` into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` (rejected — this was the bug:
  the image substitutes only `*.template` files from `/etc/nginx/templates`).
- Full envsubst without filter (rejected — nginx's own `$variables` would be
  eaten wherever an env var shares the name).
- `$$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` as an nginx variable fed from the environment
  (rejected — nginx never exposes env vars; only templates substitute).
- sed/templating in our own entrypoint wrapper (rejected — reinvents what
  the official image already does, adds a build dependency).
```

```python
"""Guard: the nginx config ships as an envsubst template that renders exactly
like the official image does it, and compose mounts it as a template.

Real-stack bug 2026-11-16 (after cuts F1–F7): nginx/nginx.conf was mounted
straight into /etc/nginx/conf.d/ while carrying a literal `$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN`;
the nginx image substitutes env vars ONLY into files from
/etc/nginx/templates/*.template, so the placeholder survived, nginx treated
it as its own variable and died on every start:
  [emerg] 1#1: unknown "csp_media_origin" variable

The renderer below mirrors docker-nginx's entrypoint
(20-envsubst-on-templates.sh): env vars matching NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER are
substituted, everything else stays literal for nginx.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TEMPLATE_PATH = ROOT / "nginx" / "default.conf.template"
COMPOSE_PATH = ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"

# nginx image: NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER selects which env vars are substituted.
ENVSUBST_FILTER_SOURCE = "^CSP_"
_ENVSUBST_FILTER = re.compile(ENVSUBST_FILTER_SOURCE)

# Every $variable the rendered config may keep — nginx's own variables.
NGINX_VARIABLES = frozenset({
    "binary_remote_addr", "http_host", "http_range", "proxy_add_x_forwarded_for",
    "remote_addr", "scheme",
})

# Substitute ${NAME} and $NAME like `envsubst '${CSP_A} ${CSP_B}'`.
_VAR = re.compile(r"\$(?:\{(?P<braced>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|(?P<bare>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*))")

DEFAULT_ENV = {"CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN": "http://localhost"}
...
```

1: # ADR-007: Frontend — SSR Jinja2 + small external JS, no bundler, no CDN
2: 
3: Status: accepted (2026-11-15). Context: owner task m02359 — simple frontend that
4: looks and lays out like YouTube (graded on similarity), deployed on a clean VM
5: without extra dependencies; own name/logo, no trademark copying.
6: 
7: ## Decision
8: 
9: Server-side rendering with **Jinja2 inside FastAPI** (`src/app/pages.py` +
10: `src/app/templates/*.html`), plus a small amount of **vanilla JS in external
11: files** under `src/app/static/*.js` (served same-origin via `app.mount("/static")`).
12: No build step, no bundler, no frontend framework.
13: 
14: Consequences / rules:
15: 
16: 1. **No external CDN, fonts, or scripts.** All static assets, icons (inline
17:    SVG in templates), and the system font stack live in the repo. A guard test
18:    (`tests/test_frontend_f7.py::test_no_external_urls_in_templates_and_static`)
19:    fails the build if any `http(s)://` URL other than localhost appears in
20:    templates or static files.
21: 2. **CSP-ready**: no inline `<script>` and no `on*=` handlers anywhere (guard
22:    test included); every JS file is external, so nginx sends
23:    `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; ...`
24:    (media-src also allows `$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` for presigned video URLs).
25: 3. **No `|safe`** for user data — Jinja autoescape stays on; XSS tests pin
26:    escaping of video titles, descriptions, channel names, comment text.
27: 4. **JS talks to the API same-origin** via `fetch` (`window.tzApi` in
28:    `app.js`); the session cookie rides along; API error `detail` strings are
29:    shown to the user in Russian in a toast/error box. XHR is used only for
30:    upload progress events (`upload.js`).
31: 5. **Themes**: CSS custom properties in `app.css`; light default,
32:    `[data-theme="dark"]` override, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
33:    fallback; `theme.js` (loaded in `<head>`) sets `data-theme` from
34:    localStorage or the media query before first paint; header toggle button
35:    flips it.
36: 6. **Layout** (YouTube-like): sticky top bar (menu button, logo, search box,
37:    upload button, theme toggle, avatar/login), collapsible left sidebar
38:    (Главная, Подписки, Вы, + Модерация for staff), responsive grid of 16:9
39:    cards (thumbnail, duration badge, avatar, title, channel, views·date),
40:    chips row on the home page. Watch page: two columns — player + title +
41:    channel row with subscribe button + like/dislike segmented control +
42:    description + comments; right column recommendations. Channel page: header
43:    (avatar, name, counters, description, subscribe/edit) + tabs
44:    «Видео»/«Плейлисты».
45: 7. **HTML error pages** (`error.html`) for 403/404/500 on browser routes via
46:    exception handlers in `main.py`; `/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/docs` and JSON
47:    clients keep JSON error bodies.
48: 8. **Branding**: own name "TZ Video" with a simple red play-button SVG logo;
49:    no YouTube trademarks, names, or assets.
50: 
51: ## Alternatives considered
52: 
53: - SPA (React/Vue) + bundler: rejected — needs a build step and node_modules at
54:   deploy time; violates "clean VM, no extra deps" and complicates CSP.
55: - CDN fonts/icons (e.g. Google Fonts): rejected — external requests break on a
56:   clean VM and violate the no-external-URL rule.
57: - Inline scripts: rejected — blocks `script-src 'self'`.
58: 
59: ## Pages & JS modules
60: 
61: | Page | Route | Template | JS |
62: |---|---|---|---|
63: | Home feed | `/` | home.html (+_cards.html) | app.js |
64: | Search | `/search?q=` | home.html | app.js |
65: | Login/Register | `/login`, `/register` | auth.html | auth.js |
66: | Watch | `/watch/{id}` | watch.html | watch.js |
67: | Upload | `/upload` | upload.html | upload.js |
68: | My videos | `/me/videos` | my_videos.html | manage.js |
69: | Channel | `/channel/{id}?tab=` | channel.html (+_cards.html) | channel.js |
70: | Subscriptions | `/subscriptions` | subs.html | — |
71: | Playlist | `/playlist/{id}` | playlist.html | playlist.js |
72: | Moderation | `/mod` | mod.html | mod.js |
73: | Errors | any | error.html | — |

{"file_path":"F:\programms\github\tzyoutube\docs\adr\ADR-008-nginx-config-envsubst.md","content":"# ADR-008: nginx config as envsubst template, substitution limited to `CSP_`

Status: accepted (2026-11-16). Context: real-stack check after cuts F1–F7 —
nginx restart-loops, site down, `[emerg] 1#1: unknown "csp_media_origin"
variable`; `20-envsubst-on-templates.sh` in the entrypoint ran idle because
no `*.template` file existed. Other containers were fine, migrations applied.

## Decision

The nginx site config ships as a **template rendered by the official image's
own entrypoint**, not as a ready-to-use config:

1. `nginx/default.conf.template` is mounted read-only at
   `/etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template`; the entrypoint
   (`20-envsubst-on-templates.sh`) renders it to
   `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` on every start.
2. **`NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_`** — only variables whose names start with
   `CSP_` are substituted. All nginx variables (`$host`, `$remote_addr`,
   `$http_host`, `$scheme`, `$binary_remote_addr`, `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`,
   `$http_range`) stay literal for nginx.
3. **The scheme is never hardcoded.** `docker-compose.yml` assembles the
   browser-visible media origin from two variables:
   `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN=<CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME>://<S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT>` (endpoint may
   carry `:port`). Defaults are `http` + `localhost`, so a local
   `docker compose up` without `deploy.sh`/`.env` works out of the box; on the
   VM `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=https` covers TLS offloading. `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` is
   the single source of the browser-visible storage host (same value the
   presigned-URL client gets from the app).

Consequences / rules:

1. Guard test `tests/test_nginx_template_render.py` renders the template the
   way the container does (substitution restricted by the filter) and fails on
   unexpanded `${...}`, unknown nginx variables, a mount straight into
   `/etc/nginx/conf.d/`, or a hardcoded scheme in the CSP header. `nginx -t`
   on the rendered config lives behind the `integration` marker.
2. Values reaching nginx are exactly the compose-composed `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN`;
   if it were unset, envsubst would substitute an empty string — the guard
   renders with explicit envs so an empty origin cannot ship silently.
3. The previous failure mode is structurally impossible: a mount target of
   `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` would leave `${CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN}` literal, and the
   guard forbids that mount target.
4. The CSP header value is defined in one place (the template). Directive set:
   `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'
   data:; media-src 'self' <origin>; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self';
   form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none';
   base-uri 'self'`.

## Alternatives considered

- Mount `nginx.conf` directly into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` (rejected — this was
  the bug: the image substitutes env vars only into files from
  `/etc/nginx/templates/*.template`).
- `envsubst` the whole file without a filter (rejected — it would eat every
  `$variable` whose name matches any environment variable, breaking nginx
  variables like `$host` and `$remote_addr`).
- Declare `$$CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN` as an nginx variable fed from the environment
  (rejected — nginx never exposes environment variables as nginx variables;
  only the template mechanism substitutes them).
- Own entrypoint wrapper with sed (rejected — reinvents what the official
  image entrypoint already does, adds a build dependency)."}

1: # Reverse proxy: the only published port. Proxies / to the web service,
2: # /videos/ and /thumbnails/ to the S3 storage (Silo; signature host
3: # validation, no rewrite).
4: #
5: # Presigned URLs are signed for the PUBLIC host (S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT).
6: # Silo validates the SigV4 signature against the Host header, so every
7: # silo location must forward Host EXACTLY as the browser sent it
8: # ($http_host, with port). Changing this to $host drops the port and
9: # breaks signature validation.
10: 
11: # C5: IP-level rate limiting for the auth endpoints. The app layers its
12: # own per-account limits (register/login) on top; this is the perimeter.
13: # This file is mounted at /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf (http context).
14: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=auth_per_ip:10m rate=10r/m;
15: 
16: server {
17:     listen 80;
18: 
19:     # C5: default body cap for everything; ONLY the upload location below
20:     # overrides it to 512m (must match MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE in the app).
21:     client_max_body_size 10m;
22: 
23:     # C5: baseline security headers on every response. Inherited by all
24:     # locations EXCEPT /media/thumbnails/, which declares its own add_header
25:     # (Cache-Control) and therefore re-declares these three itself.
26:     add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always;
27:     add_header X-Frame-Options DENY always;
28:     add_header Referrer-Policy no-referrer-when-downgrade always;
29: 
30:     # F1 (ADR-007): CSP allows ONLY same-origin scripts/styles — every JS
31:     # file is external (/static/*.js), there are no inline handlers, so
32:     # script-src 'self' holds. Media may also come from the presign host
33:     # ($CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN is set from S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT in compose; nginx
34:     # exposes env vars as variables by default, unset -> empty).
35:     add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self' $CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'" always;
36: 
37:     # C5: auth endpoints (bcrypt cost 12) are rate-limited at the proxy too.
38:     location /auth/ {
39:         limit_req zone=auth_per_ip burst=20 nodelay;
40:         proxy_pass http://web:8000;

42:         proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
43:         proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;

3: # validation, no rewrite).
4: #
5: # Presigned URLs are signed for the PUBLIC host (S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT).
6: # Silo validates the SigV4 signature against the Host header, so every
7: # silo location must forward Host EXACTLY as the browser sent it
8: # ($http_host, with port). Changing this to $host drops the port and
9: # breaks signature validation.

12: # own per-account limits (register/login) on top; this is the perimeter.

14: # /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template, the nginx image entrypoint
15: # renders it to /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf on start, substituting ONLY
16: # variables matching NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_ (ADR-008). Every other
17: # $variable below is nginx's own and must NOT be substituted.
18: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=auth_per_ip:10m rate=10r/m;
19: 
20: server {
21:     listen 80;
22:

24:     # overrides it to 512m (must match MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE in the app).
25:     client_max_body_size 10m;
26: 
27:     # C5: baseline security headers on every response. Inherited by all
28:     # locations EXCEPT /media/thumbnails/, which declares its own add_header

Important: `depends_on:\n      - web` in the fixed version — I wrote it. Wait, in my edit I kept `depends_on:\n      - web` as-is. Hmm — but task 5 wants healthcheck etc. — that's a later commit. OK.

One concern: compose's variable interpolation reads `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME` from the shell/.env — the value `"${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}"` reads from the HOST environment, and we also define CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in the nginx service environment so the CONTAINER gets CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=http (needed for the CSP_ filter to substitute only CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN — harmless).

Hmm wait — subtlety: `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN: "${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}://${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}"` — the ${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http} inside is interpolated by COMPOSE itself from host env, producing e.g. "http://localhost". Good. Note deploy.sh sets S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT etc. in .env; CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME comes from .env if present.

Also — CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in .env.example → documented.

Now edit .env.example (add after S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT block, before Limits, lines 22-27; insert after line 22 area).

- Интеграционные тесты требуют PostgreSQL/Silo/Redis — помечены маркером `@pytest.mark.integration`, запускаются только после вашего подтверждения (см. рабочие правила).
- Порядок работы: тесты → код (red-green). Для задач, где тест не имеет смысла (шаблоны, конфиги NGINX), — ручная проверка с чек-листом. Исключение — конфиг NGINX: `tests/test_nginx_template_render.py` рендерит `nginx/default.conf.template` так же, как контейнер (envsubst с фильтром `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^CSP_`), и требует: нет нераскрытых `${...}`, неизвестных nginx-переменных и имени в комментарии отсутствующего в конфиге (например `csp_media_origin` после комментария `$variable`), `$host`/`$remote_addr`/`$scheme`/`$http_range` на месте, в CSP реальный адрес хранилища, в compose нет монтирования в `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` и есть монтирование в `/etc/nginx/templates/` (ADR-008). `nginx -t` по отрендеренному конфигу — под маркером `integration`, если бинарник есть в системе.
  - Тест содержит `_strip_comment_lines`: конструкции вида `$host` в тексте комментария nginx не обрабатывает, поэтому проверка имён переменных идёт только по директивам.
- Ручные проверки: формат «команда → ожидаемый результат → что прислать обратно».

Important: `depends_on:\n      - web` in the fixed version — I wrote it. Wait, in my edit I kept `depends_on:\n      - web` as-is. Hmm — but task 5 wants healthcheck etc. — that's a later commit. OK.

One concern: compose's variable interpolation reads `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME` from the shell/.env — the value `"${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}"` reads from the HOST environment, and we also define CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in the nginx service environment so the CONTAINER gets CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=http (needed for the CSP_ filter to substitute only CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN — harmless).

Hmm wait — subtlety: `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN: "${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}://${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}"` — the ${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http} inside is interpolated by COMPOSE itself from host env, producing e.g. "http://localhost". Good. Note deploy.sh sets S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT etc. in .env; CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME comes from .env if present.

Also — CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in .env.example → documented.

Now edit .env.example (add after S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT block, before Limits, lines 22-27; insert after line 22 area).

Wait — that docs/testing.md edit added a second bullet that duplicates text awkwardly. Let me re-read it... The added sub-bullet says "Тест содержит `_strip_comment_lines`: конструкции вида `$host` в тексте комментария nginx не обрабатывает, поэтому проверка имён переменных идёт только по директивам." Hmm — this is redundant and wordy; the main line got cluttered with "и имени в комментарии отсутствующего в конфиге (например `csp_media_origin` после комментария `$variable`)" — that phrasing is garbled Russian. Let me reconsider.

The test strips comment lines entirely, so variables in comments are ignored — meaning "unknown nginx variables in comments" are NOT checked. My intended claim in testing.md should simply say the unknown-variable check covers directives. Let me clean the whole line back to a simpler, correct statement, dropping the confusing sub-bullet.

Important: `depends_on:\n      - web` in the fixed version — I wrote it. Wait, in my edit I kept `depends_on:\n      - web` as-is. Hmm — but task 5 wants healthcheck etc. — that's a later commit. OK.

One concern: compose's variable interpolation reads `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME` from the shell/.env — the value `"${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}"` reads from the HOST environment, and we also define CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in the nginx service environment so the CONTAINER gets CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=http (needed for the CSP_ filter to substitute only CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN — harmless).

Hmm wait — subtlety: `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN: "${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}://${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}"` — the ${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http} inside is interpolated by COMPOSE itself from host env, producing e.g. "http://localhost". Good. Note deploy.sh sets S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT etc. in .env; CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME comes from .env if present.

Also — CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in .env.example → documented.

Now edit .env.example (add after S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT block, before Limits, lines 22-27; insert after line 22 area).

Wait — that docs/testing.md edit added a second bullet that duplicates text awkwardly. Let me re-read it... The added sub-bullet says "Тест содержит `_strip_comment_lines`: конструкции вида `$host` в тексте комментария nginx не обрабатывает, поэтому проверка имён переменных идёт только по директивам." Hmm — this is redundant and wordy; the main line got cluttered with "и имени в комментарии отсутствующего в конфиге (например `csp_media_origin` после комментария `$variable`)" — that phrasing is garbled Russian. Let me reconsider.

The test strips comment lines entirely, so variables in comments are ignored — meaning "unknown nginx variables in comments" are NOT checked. My intended claim in testing.md should simply say the unknown-variable check covers directives. Let me clean the whole line back to a simpler, correct statement, dropping the confusing sub-bullet.

Important: `depends_on:\n      - web` in the fixed version — I wrote it. Wait, in my edit I kept `depends_on:\n      - web` as-is. Hmm — but task 5 wants healthcheck etc. — that's a later commit. OK.

One concern: compose's variable interpolation reads `CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME` from the shell/.env — the value `"${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}"` reads from the HOST environment, and we also define CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in the nginx service environment so the CONTAINER gets CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME=http (needed for the CSP_ filter to substitute only CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN — harmless).

Hmm wait — subtlety: `CSP_MEDIA_ORIGIN: "${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http}://${S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT:-localhost}"` — the ${CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME:-http} inside is interpolated by COMPOSE itself from host env, producing e.g. "http://localhost". Good. Note deploy.sh sets S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT etc. in .env; CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME comes from .env if present.

Also — CSP_MEDIA_SCHEME in .env.example → documented.

Now edit .env.example (add after S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT block, before Limits, lines 22-27; insert after line 22 area).

Wait — that docs/testing.md edit added a second bullet that duplicates text awkwardly. Let me re-read it... The added sub-bullet says "Тест содержит `_strip_comment_lines`: конструкции вида `$host` в тексте комментария nginx не обрабатывает, поэтому проверка имён переменных идёт только по директивам." Hmm — this is redundant and wordy; the main line got cluttered with "и имени в комментарии отсутствующего в конфиге (например `csp_media_origin` после комментария `$variable`)" — that phrasing is garbled Russian. Let me reconsider.

The test strips comment lines entirely, so variables in comments are ignored — meaning "unknown nginx variables in comments" are NOT checked. My intended claim in testing.md should simply say the unknown-variable check covers directives. Let me clean the whole line back to a simpler, correct statement, dropping the confusing sub-bullet.
